title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
description: All six CSF 2.0 Functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) and their 106 Subcategories as defences set to todo, under the threats they address. The Risk Assessment Category, ID.RA, asks for what an assessment like this one records: threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts, used to prioritise responses. Choose the outcomes you target with a CSF Profile and shelve the rest. Descriptions summarise NIST CSWP 29; they are not its text.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risk accepted without anyone deciding to
risks.description: Decisions about systems, suppliers and data are taken without knowing the cybersecurity risk they carry, so losses, contractual penalties and regulatory action follow from risks nobody chose to accept.

risks.title: Theft, exposure or corruption of data
risks.description: Confidential, personal or business-critical data is stolen, disclosed or altered, with notification, liability and reputational costs.

risks.title: Disruption of critical services and operations
risks.description: Systems the organization or its customers depend on stop or degrade, through attack or failure, for longer than the business can tolerate.

attacks.title: Nobody owns or steers cybersecurity risk
attacks.description: Leadership has set no risk appetite, roles and policy are unclear, and nobody reviews whether the strategy works.

attacks.title: Risks are not identified or assessed before they are taken
attacks.description: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts are not recorded, so responses are not prioritised and changes go ahead unassessed.

attacks.title: Unknown or unmanaged assets are exploited
attacks.description: Hardware, software, services or data the organization does not know it has go unpatched and unmonitored, and become the way in.

attacks.title: Compromise or failure through a supplier
attacks.description: A supplier, service provider or acquired product is compromised or fails, and the organization inherits the incident.

attacks.title: Credential theft and unauthorized access
attacks.description: Stolen, guessed or over-privileged accounts give an attacker access to systems and data.

attacks.title: Phishing and social engineering of staff
attacks.description: People are tricked into giving away credentials, running malware or making payments.

attacks.title: Exploitation of vulnerabilities and insecure configuration
attacks.description: Unpatched software, insecure defaults or flaws in in-house code are exploited.

attacks.title: Data exposed or exfiltrated
attacks.description: Data at rest, in transit or in use is read or copied by someone who should not have it.

attacks.title: Physical access to facilities or equipment
attacks.description: Someone gains physical access to premises, devices or media and tampers with or takes them.

attacks.title: Ransomware or destructive malware
attacks.description: Malware encrypts or destroys systems and data and halts operations.

attacks.title: Infrastructure failure, overload or environmental event
attacks.description: Power, hardware, capacity or a fire or flood takes systems down without any attacker.

attacks.title: Attacker activity goes undetected
attacks.description: Nothing is logged or watched closely enough to notice an intrusion until its damage is done.

attacks.title: An incident is handled poorly and escalates
attacks.description: An incident is not triaged, contained or communicated in time, so it spreads and its cost grows.

attacks.title: Recovery fails or takes too long
attacks.description: Backups are missing or tainted and there is no tested way back to normal operation.

defences.title: GV.OC-01 Mission informs cybersecurity risk management
defences.description: Risk decisions start from what the organization exists to do, so protection follows what matters to the mission.

defences.title: GV.OC-02 Stakeholder needs and expectations understood
defences.description: The cybersecurity expectations of customers, staff, owners, regulators and partners are known and taken into account.

defences.title: GV.OC-03 Legal, regulatory and contractual requirements managed
defences.description: Obligations on cybersecurity, privacy and civil liberties are identified, tracked and met.

defences.title: GV.OC-04 What others depend on from us is understood
defences.description: The objectives, capabilities and services customers and partners rely on are known and communicated, so their protection is prioritised.

defences.title: GV.OC-05 What we depend on is understood
defences.description: The outcomes, capabilities and services the organization itself depends on, including from suppliers, are known and communicated.

defences.title: GV.RM-01 Risk management objectives agreed
defences.description: Stakeholders agree what cybersecurity risk management is meant to achieve.

defences.title: GV.RM-02 Risk appetite and tolerance stated
defences.description: How much cybersecurity risk the organization will accept is written down, communicated and kept current.

defences.title: GV.RM-03 Cybersecurity part of enterprise risk management
defences.description: Cybersecurity risks and their outcomes are handled in the same enterprise risk process as other risks.

defences.title: GV.RM-04 Risk response options set out
defences.description: The strategy says which responses (mitigate, transfer, avoid, accept) are appropriate and when.

defences.title: GV.RM-05 Lines of communication for cybersecurity risk
defences.description: Risks, including those from suppliers and third parties, have clear routes to the people who decide on them.

defences.title: GV.RM-06 Standard method for calculating and prioritising risk
defences.description: One documented method is used to calculate, document, categorise and prioritise cybersecurity risks, so results can be compared.

defences.title: GV.RM-07 Strategic opportunities considered
defences.description: Positive risks, opportunities a cybersecurity capability opens up, are part of the risk discussion.

defences.title: GV.RR-01 Leadership accountable for cybersecurity risk
defences.description: Leaders own cybersecurity risk and build a culture that is risk-aware, ethical and keeps improving.

defences.title: GV.RR-02 Roles, responsibilities and authorities established
defences.description: Who does what in cybersecurity risk management is defined, communicated, understood and enforced.

defences.title: GV.RR-03 Resources match the risk strategy
defences.description: Budget, people and tools are allocated in proportion to the strategy, roles and policies.

defences.title: GV.RR-04 Cybersecurity in human resources practices
defences.description: Screening, onboarding, role changes and offboarding include cybersecurity.

defences.title: GV.PO-01 Cybersecurity policy established and enforced
defences.description: A policy for managing cybersecurity risk, based on context, strategy and priorities, is communicated and enforced.

defences.title: GV.PO-02 Policy reviewed and kept current
defences.description: The policy is updated as requirements, threats, technology and the mission change.

defences.title: GV.OV-01 Strategy outcomes reviewed
defences.description: The results of the risk management strategy are reviewed to adjust its direction.

defences.title: GV.OV-02 Strategy coverage reviewed
defences.description: The strategy is checked against the organization's requirements and risks and adjusted where it falls short.

defences.title: GV.OV-03 Risk management performance evaluated
defences.description: How well cybersecurity risk management performs is measured and reviewed for needed changes.

defences.title: GV.SC-01 Supply chain risk management programme
defences.description: A programme with strategy, objectives, policies and processes for cybersecurity supply chain risk is agreed.

defences.title: GV.SC-02 Supplier roles and responsibilities coordinated
defences.description: Cybersecurity roles for suppliers, customers and partners are set and coordinated inside and outside the organization.

defences.title: GV.SC-03 Supply chain risk integrated into risk management
defences.description: Supply chain risk is part of cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment and improvement.

defences.title: GV.SC-04 Suppliers known and prioritised by criticality
defences.description: Every supplier is known and ranked by how much the organization depends on it.

defences.title: GV.SC-05 Cybersecurity requirements in supplier contracts
defences.description: Requirements addressing supply chain risk are prioritised and written into contracts and agreements.

defences.title: GV.SC-06 Due diligence before engaging a supplier
defences.description: Planning and due diligence reduce risk before a supplier or third-party relationship begins.

defences.title: GV.SC-07 Supplier risk managed through the relationship
defences.description: Risks from a supplier and its products and services are recorded, assessed, responded to and monitored for as long as the relationship lasts.

defences.title: GV.SC-08 Suppliers included in incident planning
defences.description: Relevant suppliers take part in incident planning, response and recovery.

defences.title: GV.SC-09 Supply chain practices monitored across the life cycle
defences.description: Supply chain security practices are part of the risk programmes and their performance is tracked through the product and service life cycle.

defences.title: GV.SC-10 Provisions for after a supplier relationship ends
defences.description: Plans cover what happens when a partnership or service ends: access removed, data returned or destroyed.

defences.title: ID.AM-01 Hardware inventory maintained
defences.description: An up-to-date inventory of the hardware the organization manages.

defences.title: ID.AM-02 Software, services and systems inventory maintained
defences.description: An up-to-date inventory of the software, services and systems the organization manages.

defences.title: ID.AM-03 Network communication and data flows documented
defences.description: Authorised network communication and internal and external data flows are mapped and kept current.

defences.title: ID.AM-04 Inventory of supplier services maintained
defences.description: The services suppliers provide are inventoried.

defences.title: ID.AM-05 Assets prioritised by criticality and impact
defences.description: Assets are ranked by classification, criticality, resources and impact on the mission.

defences.title: ID.AM-07 Data inventory maintained
defences.description: Designated types of data, and their metadata, are inventoried.

defences.title: ID.AM-08 Assets managed throughout their life cycle
defences.description: Systems, hardware, software, services and data are managed from acquisition to disposal.

defences.title: ID.RA-01 Vulnerabilities identified, validated and recorded
defences.description: Vulnerabilities in assets are found, confirmed and recorded, by scanning, testing and review.

defences.title: ID.RA-02 Threat intelligence received
defences.description: Cyber threat intelligence comes in from information-sharing forums and sources.

defences.title: ID.RA-03 Internal and external threats identified and recorded
defences.description: The threats facing the organization are identified and recorded. In an assessment like this one, the attacks are that record.

defences.title: ID.RA-04 Impacts and likelihoods identified and recorded
defences.description: How likely each threat is to exploit a vulnerability, and what it would cost, are estimated and recorded: here, the values on risks and attacks.

defences.title: ID.RA-05 Inherent risk understood and used to prioritise
defences.description: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts are combined into inherent risk, which ranks the responses.

defences.title: ID.RA-06 Risk responses chosen, planned and tracked
defences.description: Responses are chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked and communicated: here, defences with their status.

defences.title: ID.RA-07 Changes and exceptions assessed and tracked
defences.description: Changes and exceptions are assessed for their risk impact, recorded and tracked.

defences.title: ID.RA-08 Vulnerability disclosure process
defences.description: There is a process to receive, analyse and respond to vulnerabilities reported by others.

defences.title: ID.RA-09 Hardware and software checked before use
defences.description: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed before they are acquired and used.

defences.title: ID.RA-10 Critical suppliers assessed before acquisition
defences.description: Critical suppliers are assessed before the organization commits to them.

defences.title: ID.IM-01 Improvements identified from evaluations
defences.description: Audits, assessments and reviews lead to recorded improvements.

defences.title: ID.IM-02 Improvements identified from tests and exercises
defences.description: Security tests and exercises, including with suppliers, lead to recorded improvements.

defences.title: ID.IM-03 Improvements identified from operations
defences.description: Running processes and activities day to day surfaces improvements that are acted on.

defences.title: ID.IM-04 Incident response and other plans maintained
defences.description: Incident response plans and other plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained and improved.

defences.title: PR.AA-01 Identities and credentials managed
defences.description: Identities and credentials for users, services and hardware are issued, managed and revoked by the organization.

defences.title: PR.AA-02 Identities proofed and bound to credentials
defences.description: Identities are verified and bound to credentials to a degree that suits the interaction.

defences.title: PR.AA-03 Users, services and hardware authenticated
defences.description: Everything that connects is authenticated, with multi-factor authentication where the risk calls for it.

defences.title: PR.AA-04 Identity assertions protected and verified
defences.description: Tokens and other identity assertions, as in single sign-on, are protected, conveyed and verified.

defences.title: PR.AA-05 Least privilege and separation of duties
defences.description: Access permissions are defined in policy, enforced and reviewed, on the principles of least privilege and separation of duties.

defences.title: PR.AA-06 Physical access managed and monitored
defences.description: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored and enforced in proportion to the risk.

defences.title: PR.AT-01 Awareness and training for all personnel
defences.description: Everyone gets the awareness and training to do their work with cybersecurity risk in mind.

defences.title: PR.AT-02 Training for specialised roles
defences.description: People in specialised roles, such as administrators, developers and executives, get training for the risks of their role.

defences.title: PR.DS-01 Data at rest protected
defences.description: Stored data is protected, for example by encryption and integrity checks.

defences.title: PR.DS-02 Data in transit protected
defences.description: Data moving over networks is protected, for example by encryption.

defences.title: PR.DS-10 Data in use protected
defences.description: Data being processed is protected, for example by isolation and access control in memory.

defences.title: PR.DS-11 Backups created, protected and tested
defences.description: Backups are made, kept safe from tampering and tested by restoring them.

defences.title: PR.PS-01 Configuration management
defences.description: Secure configuration baselines are set, applied and kept under change control.

defences.title: PR.PS-02 Software maintained, replaced and removed
defences.description: Software is patched, replaced and removed in proportion to the risk.

defences.title: PR.PS-03 Hardware maintained, replaced and removed
defences.description: Hardware is maintained, replaced and disposed of in proportion to the risk.

defences.title: PR.PS-04 Logs generated for continuous monitoring
defences.description: Systems produce log records and make them available for monitoring.

defences.title: PR.PS-05 Unauthorised software prevented
defences.description: Installing and running unauthorised software is prevented.

defences.title: PR.PS-06 Secure software development
defences.description: Secure development practices are part of the software life cycle, and how well they work is monitored.

defences.title: PR.IR-01 Networks protected from unauthorised access
defences.description: Networks and environments are segmented and protected from unauthorised logical access and use.

defences.title: PR.IR-02 Assets protected from environmental threats
defences.description: Technology assets are protected from fire, flood, power loss and similar hazards.

defences.title: PR.IR-03 Resilience mechanisms in normal and adverse conditions
defences.description: Redundancy, failover and similar mechanisms meet the resilience requirements.

defences.title: PR.IR-04 Adequate capacity maintained
defences.description: Enough resource capacity is kept to ensure availability.

defences.title: DE.CM-01 Networks monitored
defences.description: Networks and network services are monitored for potentially adverse events.

defences.title: DE.CM-02 Physical environment monitored
defences.description: The physical environment is monitored for potentially adverse events.

defences.title: DE.CM-03 Personnel activity and technology use monitored
defences.description: What people do and how technology is used are monitored for potentially adverse events.

defences.title: DE.CM-06 External service providers monitored
defences.description: The activities and services of external providers are monitored for potentially adverse events.

defences.title: DE.CM-09 Hardware, software and runtime monitored
defences.description: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments and their data are monitored for potentially adverse events.

defences.title: DE.AE-02 Adverse events analysed
defences.description: Potentially adverse events are analysed to understand the activity behind them.

defences.title: DE.AE-03 Information correlated from multiple sources
defences.description: Events from different sources are correlated to reveal what no single source shows.

defences.title: DE.AE-04 Impact and scope of adverse events understood
defences.description: The likely impact and scope of an adverse event are estimated.

defences.title: DE.AE-06 Adverse event information shared with staff and tools
defences.description: Information on adverse events reaches the authorised people and tools that need it.

defences.title: DE.AE-07 Threat intelligence used in analysis
defences.description: Threat intelligence and other context are part of the analysis.

defences.title: DE.AE-08 Incidents declared on defined criteria
defences.description: An incident is declared when adverse events meet criteria defined in advance.

defences.title: RS.MA-01 Incident response plan executed with third parties
defences.description: Once an incident is declared, the response plan is executed together with relevant third parties.

defences.title: RS.MA-02 Incident reports triaged and validated
defences.description: Incident reports are triaged and confirmed.

defences.title: RS.MA-03 Incidents categorised and prioritised
defences.description: Incidents are categorised and prioritised so the worst are handled first.

defences.title: RS.MA-04 Incidents escalated as needed
defences.description: Incidents are escalated to the right level when they need to be.

defences.title: RS.MA-05 Criteria for starting recovery applied
defences.description: Recovery starts when the criteria for it are met, not by improvisation.

defences.title: RS.AN-03 What happened and root cause established
defences.description: Analysis establishes what took place during the incident and its root cause.

defences.title: RS.AN-06 Investigation actions recorded with integrity
defences.description: Actions taken during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance preserved.

defences.title: RS.AN-07 Incident data collected with integrity
defences.description: Incident data and metadata are collected and their integrity and provenance preserved, for forensics.

defences.title: RS.AN-08 Incident magnitude estimated and validated
defences.description: How large an incident is, is estimated and confirmed.

defences.title: RS.CO-02 Stakeholders notified of incidents
defences.description: Internal and external stakeholders, including regulators where required, are notified of incidents.

defences.title: RS.CO-03 Information shared with designated stakeholders
defences.description: Information about the incident is shared with the designated internal and external stakeholders.

defences.title: RS.MI-01 Incidents contained
defences.description: Incidents are contained to stop them spreading.

defences.title: RS.MI-02 Incidents eradicated
defences.description: The cause of the incident is removed from the environment.

defences.title: RC.RP-01 Recovery plan executed
defences.description: The recovery part of the incident response plan is executed once the response process starts it.

defences.title: RC.RP-02 Recovery actions selected and prioritised
defences.description: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritised and carried out.

defences.title: RC.RP-03 Backups verified before restoring
defences.description: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is checked before they are used.

defences.title: RC.RP-04 Post-incident operational norms set
defences.description: Critical mission functions and risk management shape what normal operation looks like after the incident.

defences.title: RC.RP-05 Restored assets verified and services confirmed
defences.description: Restored assets are checked for integrity, services restored and normal operation confirmed.

defences.title: RC.RP-06 End of recovery declared and documented
defences.description: Recovery ends on defined criteria and its documentation is completed.

defences.title: RC.CO-03 Recovery progress communicated
defences.description: Progress in restoring operations is communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders.

defences.title: RC.CO-04 Public updates on recovery shared
defences.description: Public updates on recovery go out through approved methods and messaging.

defences.title: Cyber insurance (risk transfer)
defences.description: A cyber policy covering incident response, restoration, business interruption and liability: one of the risk response options GV.RM-04 asks the strategy to set out. Insurers commonly ask for multi-factor authentication, tested backups and patching before they cover ransomware.
